newsitem.title: MALTA: Maltese rush for imported goods before tax changes.
newsitem.headline: Maltese rush for imported goods before tax changes.

text.p: Maltese are rushing to buy imported electrical and home appliances ahead of tax changes promised by the new government, holding back from locally-made products.
Retailers said on Tuesday some had sold out of television sets and there was strong demand for video players.
Sales started rising sharply after the Labour Party won the October 26 general election on the back of a pledge to remove Value Added Tax (VAT) and re-introduce customs duties.
"There is a strong rush for imported goods, particularly televisions and video players," said electronics and household appliance retailer Jesmond Falzon.
"People believe prices will rise if customs duties are re-introduced. The customs rate on televisions used to be 72 percent. Some importers have already run out of stock and are only taking orders."
Joseph Galea, of Standard Electronics at Hamrun, one of the Mediterranean island's biggest shopping centres, said: "We have sold out of televisions."
But demand for local goods has fallen.

Vince Farrugia of the Association of General Retailers and Traders told Reuters: "We have been getting many reports from members who produce for the local market that people are not buying or placing orders because they want VAT to be removed first."
VAT, introduced by the former Nationalist government, was at a standard rate of 15 percent on goods and services.

"No tax on locally-made goods used to be charged before (VAT), and many people believe with the removal of VAT that prices on locally-made goods, particularly furniture, will drop by 15 percent," Farrugia said.
